baseline.title: Pre-study information and procedure check
baseline.instructions: This information is used only to describe the sample and confirm that you understand the procedure. It will not reveal your experimental condition. Please answer truthfully.

items.text: I am familiar with voice assistants, voice input, or similar voice-interaction technologies.
I am usually concerned about privacy when using an online system that requires a microphone.
I am confident that I can complete a browser-based voice task without a researcher continuously present.

fields.helper: Used only to describe the sample. It will not reveal your experimental condition.

fields.text: Which accent or dialect habit best describes your spoken Mandarin?
fields.helper: Choose the closest match to how you usually speak.

options.label: Near-standard Mandarin with little dialect accent
Mandarin with a light Chaoshan dialect accent
Mandarin with a strong Chaoshan dialect accent
Mandarin with a light Cantonese accent
Mandarin with a strong Cantonese accent
Mandarin with a light accent from another dialect
Mandarin with a strong accent from another dialect
I usually speak a dialect and switch to Mandarin for this study

fields.text: Which language do you speak most often in daily life?
During the past three months, how often have you used a voice assistant or conversational voice product?
Do you have a hearing or speech condition that may affect this voice-interaction study?
When should you tap the computer page during the study?
fields.helper: Judge by your real interaction intent; do not tap extra just to create more data.

options.label: Whenever I genuinely want the system to start answering or to stop its current answer
As often as possible to create more data

fields.text: What should you do if the network, page, or phone behaves abnormally?
fields.helper: If something goes wrong, follow the on-page recovery steps first; do not try to make up data with extra taps.

options.label: Pause and follow the recovery instructions; contact the research team if the problem continues
Tap repeatedly to replace lost data
Ignore the problem and continue the timer

fields.text: How should the computer and phone enter the study?
fields.helper: The computer study page and phone companion page belong to the same session, so how you enter on both sides should match.

options.label: Use the same participant code on the computer and companion phone

daily.title: Experience in this study session
daily.instructions: Rate your actual experience in this session. 1 means strongly disagree and 7 means strongly agree.

items.text: Overall, the system responded at the times I expected during this session.
I had to devote a great deal of attention to make the system respond at appropriate times.
The system's response timing made me feel annoyed or interrupted.
I could generally predict when the system would start responding.
Interaction with the system was efficient.
Based on this experience, I would like to continue using the system.
This session made me feel fatigued.
I felt able to control when the system started or stopped responding.

open_items.text: Was there a response-timing moment in this session that stood out? Briefly describe what happened.
Did you encounter any microphone, network, phone-playback, or page problems?

final.title: Overall evaluation of this study session
final.instructions: Think about the complete session. 1 means strongly disagree and 7 means strongly agree. Each open-ended answer must contain at least 20 Chinese characters or at least 12 English words.

items.text: As the interaction progressed, the system's response timing increasingly matched my expectations.
As the interaction progressed, I liked the system more and increasingly felt that it was worth continuing to use.
As the interaction progressed, I needed less attention and effort, and interaction became easier.
As the interaction progressed, my frustration or discomfort with the system decreased.
As the interaction progressed, I better understood how to speak to the system and could better predict its response timing.
As the interaction progressed, I increasingly felt able to control when the system started or stopped responding.
As the interaction progressed, interaction with the system became more efficient.
Overall, the system's response timing matched my expectations.
Overall, I liked the system and felt it was worth continuing to use.
Overall, the interaction required little attention and effort.
Overall, interacting with the system rarely made me feel frustrated or uncomfortable.
Overall, I knew how to speak to the system and could predict its response timing.
Overall, interaction with the system was efficient.
After I finished an utterance, I could usually anticipate whether the system would start responding.
The system often started responding when I did not expect it to respond.
In similar speaking and pausing situations, the system behaved consistently in whether it responded.
I felt able to control when the system started or stopped responding.
When I tapped Answer now or Stop answering, the system acted as I expected.
When the system's response behavior changed, those changes were understandable to me.
To manage whether the system responded, I had to deliberately change how I spoke, paused, or waited.

open_items.text: What is your main overall impression of the system?
Recall the most surprising response or non-response. What happened, and what had you expected the system to do?
Describe one specific time you tapped Answer now or Stop answering. Did the tap help you regain control of the interaction? Why or why not?
What changed most noticeably in the system during this interaction, and were those changes understandable?
Did you change how you spoke, paused, or waited in order to adapt to the system? Please describe.
Did the phone conversation partner or background sound affect how you interacted?
If you continued using the system, what would you most like it to improve?

followups.text: Why did you give the response timing a relatively low score? Describe one specific situation.
Which interactions were most likely to make you feel frustrated or uncomfortable?
Why do you think the system clearly improved? Describe the specific evidence you used.
